title: Tiered concurrency fallback rules and invoice adjustment acceptance criteria
creator: Lena Morris
description:
Summary:
This ticket specifies requirements and acceptance criteria for implementing tiered concurrency fallback rules plus automated invoice adjustment logic when requests are routed to cheaper fallback variants. The feature ensures customers are billed for the actual compute used while protecting SLA guarantees and providing transparent crediting when model or capacity fallbacks occur. This PRD clarifies billing semantics, attribution windows, rollback rules, and expected UX in the Console and invoices.
background: We currently route requests across model variants and capacity tiers for reliability and cost. However, billing currently attributes charges to the original primary route, which leads to inaccurate invoices and customer disputes when automatic fallbacks route significant traffic to lower-cost variants or when canary rollouts degrade quality. Finance and Customer Success have requested: 1) deterministic rules for attributing spend when fallback/routing occurs, 2) automatic invoice adjustments or credits for significant fallback-induced delta, and 3) Console surface to explain adjustments.
goal: Define and ship a deterministic, auditable billing behavior for concurrency fallbacks that: (a) charges customers for the actual compute tier executed, (b) automatically issues invoice credits if fallback-induced spend delta exceeds configured thresholds, and (c) surfaces explanation and audit trail in the Console and invoice line items.
scope:
In scope:
- Per-caller and per-route concurrency fallback rules (primary -> fallback tiers) and how charge attribution is computed.
- Billing logic to use execution-time variant pricing for metering and invoice generation.
- Auto-crediting rules for monthly invoices when fallback spend delta > threshold (default 5% of monthly bill or $250).
- Console UI additions: per-invoice adjustment line item and per-route fallback summary for billing windows.
- Acceptance criteria and test scenarios for billing, UI, and accounting reconciliation.
Out of scope:
- Changes to public pricing page or plan-level list prices.
- Complex cross-account chargebacks and reseller invoicing (handled in separate ticket).
requirements: R1: Metering must record actual execution variant id, compute tier, and effective per-token/per-second rate for every request in the usage event stream.
R2: Routing metadata must include a fallback flag and fallback_chain (ordered list of variant ids visited) for auditability.
R3: Billing pipeline must compute per-invoice realized delta = sum(execution_cost) - sum(original_route_estimated_cost) and persist reason codes when delta != 0.

R4: If realized delta for a billing account in a monthly invoice > max(5% of invoice_total, $250), system must automatically create a credit line equal to the delta (or configurable percentage) and attach an adjustment_reason code 'AUTO_FALLBACK_CREDIT'.
R5: Console must show per-route fallback summary for each invoice window: primary route percentage, fallback routes breakdown, and adjustment line items with links to usage events (sampled).
R6: Billing export (CSV/JSON) must include fields: execution_variant_id, requested_route_id, fallback_flag, runtime_seconds, tokens_consumed, unit_price, cost, and adjustment_reason where applicable.
R7: Admin controls: tenant admins must be able to opt-out of auto-crediting within contract constraints and set custom thresholds; defaults applied for self-serve tenants.

R8: Accounting must be able to generate an auditable report for each adjustment with three artifacts: invoice snapshot before adjustment, adjustment delta calculation, and list of sampled usage events used for verification.
R9: Grace policy: credits created by auto-crediting must be visible on the next invoice and optionally issued as immediate negative invoice for customers on monthly arrears with finance approval.
R10: Security: fallback metadata and billing attribution must not leak model prompts or customer PII in public exports; only IDs and hashed samples may be included.

R11: Backfill handling: for late-arriving usage events corresponding to previous invoice windows, the billing pipeline must re-evaluate realized delta and mark adjustments as 'retroactive' with a human-readable note and audit id.
R12: Error handling: if billing pipeline fails to compute adjustments by invoice generation time, generate a placeholder adjustment record and escalate to finance ops for manual reconciliation.
R13: Telemetry: emit metrics for % of requests routed to fallback tiers, monthly count of auto-credit events, and total amount credited per tenant.
R14: Tests: unit, integration (billing pipeline with simulated fallback events), and e2e with Console rendering of adjustments must be provided.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Usage events include execution_variant_id and fallback_flag for 100% of routed requests in the integration test harness.
AC2: Billing pipeline computes realized delta for simulated tenant workloads and auto-creates credit records when delta exceeds threshold; integration tests validate credit amount and reason code.
AC3: Console displays adjustment line item on invoice view with clear explanation and link to sampled usage events for at least 90% of auto-credited invoices in staging.
AC4: Billing export contains required fields and passes Finance CSV schema validation tool without errors.
AC5: Admin opt-out toggles are respected: when opt-out enabled for a tenant, no auto-credit records are emitted and a warning flag is shown in the invoice UI.
AC6: Retroactive adjustments for backfilled events are created with 'retroactive' tag and include original invoice id; automated tests assert correct reconciliation path.
AC7: Security checks: exported usage samples are hashed and pass a privacy scan; security review sign-off provided if any un-hashed sample fields are present.
AC8: Performance: additional metering fields increase billing pipeline processing time by <5% at 99th percentile on benchmark dataset.
AC9: Observability: new metrics emitted, dashboards created, and alert defined for >0.5% of tenants receiving auto-credits in a single day (possible regression).
test_scenarios: TS1: Canary failover simulation where primary model returns 503 for 30% of requests over a 2-hour window; majority of executed requests billed at fallback variant price. Verify realized delta and auto-credit creation.

TS2: High-volume burst that routes to a cheaper pooling tier (planned autoscaling); verify that customer is billed for executed cheaper tier and no credit is issued (because cheaper was executed intentionally).

TS3: Canary rollout introduces quality regression causing automated rollback and routing to previous variant; compute realized delta between requested canary price and actual execution price and ensure credits are created if threshold met.
TS4: Backfill event arrives 7 days late impacting previous invoice; verify retroactive adjustment record and that accounting artifacts are generated.
TS5: Admin opt-out toggle on tenant prevents credit creation; verify UI shows opt-out annotation on invoice and finance export excludes adjustments.
TS6: Privacy test: exported sampled usage events contain only hashed prompt ids and no free text; pass privacy scanner.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement metering changes and billing pipeline adjustments in staging; run integration test harness with synthetic fallback workloads.
Phase 2 (pilot): enable for 3 low-risk enterprise tenants and one internal account; monitor adjustments and finance reconciliation for 2 invoice cycles.
Phase 3 (gradual): ramp to 25% of tenants (self-serve) with default thresholds; open opt-out for enterprise negotiated customers.
Phase 4 (GA): enable for all tenants; update pricing docs and send comms to customers describing invoice adjustment semantics.
Fallback: ability to disable auto-crediting globally within 24 hours if unexpected volume of credits or accounting issues observed.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect attribution leads to large credits and revenue leakage. Mitigation: Pilot on a small set of tenants and add throttles on total daily credit volume per-tenant.
Risk: Late-arriving events cause surprise retroactive adjustments. Mitigation: expose backfill window and surface retroactive tags in Console; offer export for reconciliation.
Risk: Privacy leakage in sampled usage exports. Mitigation: default to hashed samples and run security/privacy sign-off before GA.
Risk: Complexity in accounting reconciliation. Mitigation: provide accounting artifacts and run parallel-run reconciliation for two invoice cycles before making credits live.

deliverables: D1: Updated usage event schema and producer doc
D2: Billing pipeline implementation and tests
D3: Console invoice UI showing adjustment line items and links
D4: Finance reconciliation export and runbook
D5: Pilot run report and GA rollout comms
